title: Who needs a hand at home in San Diego County?
text:
When we started Marquez Family Home Care, we wanted to understand our neighbors before we knocked on a single door. Who in our community needs help at home, and what kind of help? We went to the U.S. Census Bureau’s American Community Survey for answers.
We looked at two groups we care for:
The Census doesn’t ask whether someone “needs a caregiver.” It asks about specific difficulties, and two of them line up closely with non-medical home care:
Show the R code
library(tidyverse)
library(tidycensus)
library(scales)
library(knitr)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)

# ACS 5-year vintage. 2024 = the 2020–2024 survey. Drop to 2023 if load_variables() errors.
acs_year <- 2024

# Neighborhoods we serve, grouped into four regions (ZIP code tabulation areas)
region_levels <- c("Central & North City", "Central San Diego", "South Bay", "East County")

service_zips <- service_area$zcta

if (Sys.getenv("CENSUS_API_KEY") == "") {
  stop("No Census API key found. Run tidycensus::census_api_key('YOUR_KEY', install = TRUE) and restart R.")
}

# Brand colors for charts
brand <- list(
  forest   = "#0f3e17",
  petal    = "#79b88b",
  burgundy = "#7a1f3d",
  cream    = "#fffefc",
  charcoal = "#222222",
  mist     = "#efeeeb"
)

band_labels <- c(u18 = "Under 18", a18_64 = "Adults 18–64", s65 = "Seniors 65+")
band_colors <- c("Adults 18–64" = brand$petal, "Seniors 65+" = brand$forest)
measure_labels <- c(
  any       = "Any disability",
  selfcare  = "Need personal care help",
  indliving = "Need errand help"
)

theme_marquez <- function(base_size = 12) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      text               = element_text(color = brand$charcoal),
      plot.title         = element_text(color = brand$forest, size = base_size + 3),
      plot.title.position = "plot",
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(color = brand$charcoal),
      plot.caption       = element_text(color = brand$charcoal, size = base_size - 3, hjust = 0),
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      strip.text.y       = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0, color = brand$forest, face = "bold"),
      panel.spacing.y    = unit(14, "pt"),
      axis.text          = element_text(color = brand$charcoal),
      panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = brand$mist),
      legend.position    = "top",
      legend.justification = "left",
      plot.background    = element_rect(fill = brand$cream, color = NA),
      panel.background   = element_rect(fill = brand$cream, color = NA)
    )
}
Show the R code
acs_vars <- load_variables(acs_year, "acs5", cache = TRUE) |>
  select(name, label) |>
  mutate(label = str_remove_all(label, ":"))

acs_pull <- function(level = c("county", "zcta"), table = NULL, variables = NULL) {
  level <- match.arg(level)
  args <- list(year = acs_year, survey = "acs5")
  if (!is.null(table))     args$table <- table
  if (!is.null(variables)) args$variables <- variables
  args <- if (level == "county") {
    c(args, geography = "county", state = "CA", county = "San Diego")
  } else {
    c(args, list(geography = "zcta", zcta = service_zips))
  }
  out <- do.call(get_acs, args)
  if (!is.null(table)) out <- left_join(out, acs_vars, by = c("variable" = "name"))
  out
}

last_part <- function(label) word(label, -1, sep = "!!")

age_band <- function(age) {
  case_when(
    age %in% c("Under 18 years", "5 to 17 years")                          ~ "u18",
    age %in% c("18 to 34 years", "35 to 64 years", "18 to 64 years")       ~ "a18_64",
    age %in% c("65 to 74 years", "75 years and over", "65 years and over") ~ "s65",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

# Population by age (B01001)
age_counts <- function(level) {
  acs_pull(level, table = "B01001") |>
    filter(str_count(label, "!!") == 3) |>
    mutate(
      age_txt = last_part(label),
      age_lo  = if_else(str_detect(age_txt, "^Under"), 0,
                        as.numeric(str_extract(age_txt, "\\d+")))
    ) |>
    group_by(GEOID, NAME) |>
    summarise(
      pop_total = sum(estimate),
      pop_18_64 = sum(estimate[age_lo >= 18 & age_lo < 65]),
      pop_65    = sum(estimate[age_lo >= 65]),
      pop_75    = sum(estimate[age_lo >= 75]),
      pop_85    = sum(estimate[age_lo >= 85]),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Disability / difficulty status by age band (C18108, B18106, B18107), parsed by label
status_by_age <- function(level, table, leaf_pattern, without_pattern) {
  acs_pull(level, table = table) |>
    filter(str_detect(last_part(label), leaf_pattern)) |>
    mutate(
      age  = str_extract(label, "Under 18 years|\\d+ to \\d+ years|\\d+ years and over"),
      band = age_band(age),
      has  = !str_detect(last_part(label), without_pattern)
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(band)) |>
    group_by(GEOID, band) |>
    summarise(
      with     = sum(estimate[has]),
      with_moe = moe_sum(moe[has], estimate[has]),
      universe = sum(estimate),
      .groups  = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(pct = with / universe)
}

status_long <- function(level) {
  bind_rows(
    any       = status_by_age(level, "C18108", "disability", "^No disability"),
    selfcare  = status_by_age(level, "B18106", "difficulty", "^No "),
    indliving = status_by_age(level, "B18107", "difficulty", "^No "),
    .id = "measure"
  )
}

status_wide <- function(long) {
  long |>
    select(GEOID, measure, band, with, pct) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = c(measure, band), values_from = c(with, pct),
                names_glue = "{measure}_{band}_{.value}")
}

# Seniors living alone (B09020)
living_alone <- function(level) {
  acs_pull(level, table = "B09020") |>
    group_by(GEOID) |>
    summarise(
      pop65_universe = estimate[variable == "B09020_001"],
      alone_65       = sum(estimate[str_detect(label, regex("living alone$", ignore_case = TRUE))]),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(pct_alone_65 = alone_65 / pop65_universe)
}

# Spanish spoken at home among people 65+ (B16004)
spanish_65 <- function(level) {
  acs_pull(level, table = "B16004") |>
    group_by(GEOID) |>
    summarise(
      pop65_lang = sum(estimate[str_detect(label, "!!65 years and over$")]),
      spanish_65 = sum(estimate[str_detect(label, "65 years and over!!Speak Spanish$")]),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(pct_spanish_65 = spanish_65 / pop65_lang)
}

build_profile <- function(level) {
  long <- status_long(level)
  wide <- list(age_counts(level), status_wide(long), living_alone(level), spanish_65(level)) |>
    reduce(left_join, by = "GEOID")
  list(wide = wide, long = long)
}
Show the R code
county_raw <- build_profile("county")
zip_raw    <- build_profile("zcta")

county      <- county_raw$wide
county_long <- county_raw$long
zips        <- zip_raw$wide |> left_join(service_area, by = c("GEOID" = "zcta"))
zip_long    <- zip_raw$long |> left_join(service_area, by = c("GEOID" = "zcta"))

# When the numbers were pulled from the Census API (kept with the frozen results)
data_pulled  <- Sys.Date()
pulled_label <- sprintf("%s %d, %s", format(data_pulled, "%B"),
                        as.integer(format(data_pulled, "%d")), format(data_pulled, "%Y"))
acs_label    <- paste0("American Community Survey ", acs_year - 4, "–", acs_year, " 5-year estimates")
source_caption <- paste0("Source: U.S. Census Bureau, ", acs_label, ". Data pulled ", pulled_label, ".")

title: Who needs a hand at home in San Diego County?
section: San Diego County at a glance
text:
San Diego County at a glance


507,734 residents aged 65 and older


59,830 residents aged 85 and older


136,323 adults who need errand help


122,505 seniors who live alone



Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year estimates. Data pulled from the Census on November 2, 2026.



Show the R code
tribble(
  ~` `, ~`Adults 18–64`, ~`Seniors 65+`,
  "People in the county",
    comma(county$pop_18_64), comma(county$pop_65),
  "Living with any disability",
    comma(county$any_a18_64_with), comma(county$any_s65_with),
  "Need personal care help",
    comma(county$selfcare_a18_64_with), comma(county$selfcare_s65_with),
  "Need errand help",
    comma(county$indliving_a18_64_with), comma(county$indliving_s65_with)
) |>
  kable(caption = paste0("San Diego County, ", acs_label, ". Data pulled ", pulled_label, "."))

Show the R code
county_long |>
  filter(band %in% c("a18_64", "s65")) |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure_labels[measure], levels = rev(measure_labels)),
         band    = band_labels[band]) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = pct, y = measure, fill = band)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = percent(pct, 0.1)),
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.75), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.4,
            color = brand$charcoal) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = band_colors) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL,
       title = "The need for help grows with age, but it isn't only about age") +
  labs(caption = source_caption) +
  theme_marquez()









Seniors are several times more likely than younger adults to need help with daily tasks. But because there are so many more adults under 65, younger adults with a disability are a large share of the people who need a hand at home. Home care isn’t only for grandparents.

Often the hardest part of needing help is the everyday: getting to the doctor, a hot meal, a ride to the store. Those are the moments we’re here for.

title: Who needs a hand at home in San Diego County?
text:
Neighborhood by neighborhood
We serve four parts of the county: the neighborhoods around our home base in University City, central San Diego from downtown to Mid-City and the southeast, the South Bay, and East County. Here’s how they compare.


Show the R code
zips |>
  group_by(Region = region) |>
  summarise(
    `ZIP codes`            = n(),
    `Seniors 65+`          = sum(pop_65),
    `Seniors 85+`          = sum(pop_85),
    `Living alone (65+)`       = sum(alone_65) / sum(pop65_universe),
    `Need errand help (65+)`   = sum(indliving_s65_with),
    `Need errand help (18–64)` = sum(indliving_a18_64_with),
    `Spanish at home (65+)`    = sum(spanish_65) / sum(pop65_lang),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    across(c(`Seniors 65+`, `Seniors 85+`, `Need errand help (65+)`,
             `Need errand help (18–64)`), comma),
    across(c(`Living alone (65+)`, `Spanish at home (65+)`), \(x) percent(x, 0.1))
  ) |>
  kable(align = "lrrrrrrr",
        caption = paste0("Totals for the ZIP codes we serve. ", acs_label, ". Data pulled ", pulled_label, "."))

Show the R code
# ZIP code boundaries from the Census Bureau (TIGER/Line cartographic files)
zip_geo <- get_acs(
  geography = "zcta", zcta = service_zips, variables = "B01001_001",
  year = acs_year, survey = "acs5", geometry = TRUE
) |>
  select(GEOID, geometry) |>
  st_transform(4326)

# Share of adults (18+) with an independent-living difficulty
need_rate <- zip_long |>
  filter(measure == "indliving", band %in% c("a18_64", "s65")) |>
  group_by(GEOID) |>
  summarise(need_n = sum(with), need_universe = sum(universe), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(need_pct = need_n / need_universe)

map_data <- zip_geo |>
  left_join(zips, by = "GEOID") |>
  left_join(need_rate, by = "GEOID") |>
  mutate(hover = sprintf(
    "<strong>%s · %s</strong><br><span style='opacity:.75'>%s</span><br>
     Seniors 65+: %s<br>Seniors 85+: %s<br>
     Need errand help: %s (%s of adults)<br>
     Living alone (65+): %s<br>Spanish at home (65+): %s",
    GEOID, area, region,
    comma(pop_65), comma(pop_85),
    comma(need_n), percent(need_pct, 0.1),
    percent(pct_alone_65, 0.1), percent(pct_spanish_65, 0.1)
  ) |> lapply(htmltools::HTML))

fmt_count <- labelFormat(big.mark = ",")
fmt_pct   <- labelFormat(suffix = "%", transform = \(x) round(100 * x))

brand_map <- function(var, legend_title, fmt) {
  vals <- map_data[[var]]
  pal  <- colorNumeric(c("#e1f4df", "#b1dbb8", "#4c9463", "#0f3e17"),
                       domain = vals, na.color = "#efeeeb")
  leaflet(map_data, height = 540, options = leafletOptions(scrollWheelZoom = FALSE)) |>
    # Esri light gray basemap: free, no API key needed
    addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldGrayCanvas) |>
    addPolygons(
      fillColor = pal(vals), fillOpacity = 0.85,
      color = "#fffefc", weight = 1.2,
      label = ~hover,
      labelOptions = labelOptions(direction = "auto", textsize = "13px"),
      highlightOptions = highlightOptions(weight = 3, color = "#0f3e17", bringToFront = TRUE)
    ) |>
    addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = vals, title = legend_title,
              labFormat = fmt, opacity = 0.9)
}

title: Who needs a hand at home in San Diego County?
text:
What this means for families

Many families in our area are caring for someone right now, often while working full time. A few things stood out to us:

Help with everyday tasks is the most common need. More people need errand help than need personal care help. Companionship, rides and meals matter.
Younger adults need support too. Developmental disabilities and injuries from accidents affect people at every age. The San Diego Regional Center alone serves about 41,350 people with developmental disabilities across San Diego and Imperial counties.
Language matters. In parts of the South Bay, a large share of seniors speak Spanish at home. A caregiver who speaks your loved one’s language makes care feel like home.

title: Who needs a hand at home in San Diego County?
text:
About the data

Data pulled: November 2, 2026, from the Census Bureau API.
Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2020–2024 5-year estimates (tables B01001, B18106, B18107, C18108, B09020, B16004), pulled with the tidycensus R package. Regional Center figure: San Diego Regional Center FY 2023–24 Performance Report, CA Department of Developmental Services.
People living in nursing homes aren’t included, which suits our purpose: these are people living in their own homes.
Neighborhood numbers are estimates with real margins of error, especially in smaller ZIP codes. Treat the ranking as a general picture, not an exact count.
The measures overlap. Someone who needs personal care help often needs errand help too, so the rows shouldn’t be added together.
ZIP areas are approximate. The Census uses “ZIP code tabulation areas,” which closely match, but don’t exactly equal, postal ZIP codes.

title: Who needs a hand at home in San Diego County?
text:
Why we’re building this

We didn’t start Marquez Family Home Care to compete with the agencies already caring for San Diego families. We started it because the need keeps growing. Every year, more of our neighbors reach the age when everyday tasks get harder, and more younger adults are living with a disability or recovering from an injury. Many families are already stretched thin.
Our goal is to help fill that gap, alongside everyone else doing this work, so that more people can stay safe, comfortable and independent in the homes they love.


Wondering whether your loved one could use some help?
We’re happy to talk it through, with no pressure and no obligation. Marquez Family Home Care provides non-medical support: personal care, companionship, meals, errands and respite for family caregivers.
Book a free consultation
